title: Stars and spirals
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 1964, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: NGC 1964 · constellation Lepus · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A bright, dense core sits inside a mottled oval disc, and around that disc curl distinct spiral arms speckled with bright starry regions. This is NGC 1964, a spiral galaxy roughly 70 million light-years away in the constellation Lepus, the Hare.

The galaxy shares its patch of sky with plenty of stars in our own Milky Way. The star HD 36785 sits just to the galaxy's right, with two more prominent stars, HD 36784 and TYC 5928-368-1, above it. The large, bright star below NGC 1964 is BD-22 1147. All of these are much closer to us than the galaxy.
William Herschel noticed the galaxy's brilliant center on the night of 20 November 1784, which led to its discovery and its later entry in the New General Catalog, the source of its NGC name.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (16.95 x 16.95 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 345,000 × 345,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope and combines blue and red visible-light filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The galaxy and the background galaxies are far too faint to see by eye. The instrument can record objects many millions of times fainter than the eye can detect.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla also picks up many background galaxies here. According to ESO, the instrument registers light from objects as much as 40 million times too faint for a human eye.
alt: A spiral galaxy with a bright core inside a mottled oval disc and speckled arms, surrounded by several bright foreground stars and faint background galaxies.
